correctness.rationale: For n>=5, each closed edge neighborhood is a length-4 cyclic block. A double-count gives |D|>=ceil(n/2), attained by alternating sets. At minimum size, the necessary and sufficient adjacent gap inequality d_i+d_{i+1}<=4 creates symbols e_i=2-d_i in {-1,0,1}, with e_i+e_{i+1}>=0 and sum e_i in {0,1}. Runs of nonzero signs have excess at least one, forcing either all-zero or full +/- alternation for even n, and one alternating defect run for odd n; the no-zero odd case has a unique ++ seam. Each odd run size gives k anchored gap words and hence n unmarked labeled sets; the even counts are 2 or 6. For n=3,4 all edge neighborhoods are the full vertex set and direct checks establish the same formula. The standalone independently defined actual-graph enumerator confirms all lengths 3..18; the 8-state weighted trace independently confirms counts for 5..80. These finite computations do not substitute for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The substantive claim is a complete classification, exact labeled count and rotation-orbit census of all minimum double vertex-edge dominating sets of simple cycles, not the readily derived scalar minimum. The fully accessible 2023 primary article treats general complexity and tree algorithms but supplies no such cycle census. The 2017 originating article is not represented as fully inspected: its abstract concerns broad inequalities and tree/unicyclic results, but restricted access is a real priority risk. Search of cycle-specific, double-domination, four-window binary covering, mathematical records and exact numerical signatures found no direct coverage; absence of indexed results is not taken as a uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: The 2017 originating article is directly relevant but its complete text could not be obtained through authorized non-interactive means; a tucked-away cycle statement cannot be conclusively ruled out.
The equivalent binary four-window covering-word formulation may appear under coding/constraint language in poorly indexed literature; bounded searches do not establish uniqueness.
No independent external priority audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Minimum double coverage is a natural redundancy objective for local edge monitoring on ring networks. The exact count, full gap classification and rotation-orbit census determine the entire optimum landscape, not just the known/easy scalar minimum. The exceptional two/six even-count rigidity and odd n floor((n+3)/4) growth are sharp structural phenomena explained by a single allowable alternating defect run. This supports constructing and distinguishing all cheapest deployments and is a motivated infinite-family classification.
